FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
Part one demands a perfect ten-for-ten on traffic signs before part two opens, while part two passes at eighty percent on general multiple choice [A01].
Why it matters: group testing-knowledge; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F04, sec01-F05 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: FXsec01R02
An applicant younger than eighteen must wait fifteen full days after a failed knowledge exam. After three failures, a fourth attempt requires passing classroom driver education or a DMV-approved eight-hour manual course. Adults may use that course; younger applicants need prior classroom completion. The manual course must be completed after the third failure, and its certificate goes to DMV [FXsec01R02].
Why it matters: group testing-knowledge; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F06, sec01-F08 [FXsec01R02].
Source: [FXsec01R02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
After three failures, adults may take the manual course directly, while minors may take it only after already completing classroom driver education [A01].
Why it matters: group testing-knowledge; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F09, sec01-F10 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A01
Receiving help and giving help are two separately banned acts, and seeking questions beforehand and sharing them afterward are banned as well [A01].
Why it matters: group testing-knowledge; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F11 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A01
The exam offers an audio version and many languages including American Sign Language, yet translators stay barred wherever those versions exist [A01].
Why it matters: group testing-knowledge; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F07 [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0005]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
The examiner accepts either a driver-education completion certificate or a supervised-practice checklist on form CSMA 19, with one of the two always required [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-road; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F16 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
Minors take the road test inside their driver-education course, while adults choose between a sixty-day permit hold with DMV testing or an approved course with school testing [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-road; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F17, sec01-F18 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
One road failure costs two waiting days, while a third DMV failure costs the applicant an in-vehicle training course before any fourth attempt [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-road; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F19 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: FXsec01R09
A license marked C requires the glasses or contacts needed to pass vision screening whenever you drive. A daylight-only license permits driving beginning thirty minutes after sunrise and ending thirty minutes before sunset [FXsec01R09].
Why it matters: group testing-vision; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec01-F21, sec01-F24 [FXsec01R09].
Source: [FXsec01R09 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A02
Unrestricted vision needs twenty-forty acuity with one hundred ten degrees of field, while daylight-only needs twenty-seventy acuity with seventy degrees of field [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-vision; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec01-F22, sec01-F23 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A02
Needing glasses to pass screening adds the C restriction, while laser surgery removes it only through a fresh unaided pass or a filed MED 4 report [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-vision; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F21 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A02
Form MED 4 reports a vision screening result, while publication MED 44 informs bioptic telescopic lens wearers about licensing [A02].
Why it matters: group testing-vision; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec01-F21, sec01-F25 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0006]
